texts.preamble: Also At vs Office Of The District Magistrate on 31 July, 2023 In The Court Of Ajay Goel, Presiding Officer Industrial Tribunal-01, Rouse Avenue Court, D.D.U. Marg, New Delhi. Rca Dj No. 7/23
texts.facts: This is an appeal U/s 18 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 which has been preferred by the appellant against the impugned report dated 14.02.2023 submitted by the Local Complaints Committee, hereinafter referred to as 'LCC'. 2. The girl has not concealed her name in the appeal but keeping in view the sanctity and nature of Also At vs Office Of The District Magistrate on 31 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181077684/ 1 case and the act involved, this court is refraining from mentioning the name of girl and instead of her name, letter 'X' will be mentioned for appellant. 3. The facts relevant for disposal of present appeal are that respondent No. 1 is the District Officer, Deputy Commissioner Office, Central District and respondent No. 1 is the one who received the purported complaint filed by respondent No. 3 under section 9 of the POSH Act. It is stated that respondent No. 2 is the Local Complaints Committee through its Chairperson Ms. Anupriya Ghosh and respondent No. 2 initiated the inquiry after receiving the complaint filed by respondent No. 3 and passed the report dated 14.02.2023 U/s 13 of POSH Act. 4. It is stated that appellant is a 75 years old senior citizen and is engaged in the business of packed, processed and frozen food products range under the name and style Holy Land Marketing Private Ltd. Co. It is stated that entire company was set up and was functioning as a family business solely with the funds of the appellant and other family members were operational arms of the company working without any monetary investment or contribution of their own. 5. It is stated that respondent No. 3 is the daughter in law of the appellant and erstwhile Director of the company but not a shareholder/member and she married the younger son of the appellant Late Mr. Harith Budhraja on 16.02.2009 and lived at the family residence peacefully with her husband, children and appellant and his wife. Unfortunately, appellant's younger son /husband of respondent No. 3 passed away at the young age of 42, during 2nd wage of Covid-19 pandemic and after his demise also, the respondent No. 3 and her children continued to live peacefully with appellant and his wife. 6. It is stated that respondent No. 3 was earlier working but pursuant to birth of first child in 2011, she decided to quit job. Later on, in the year 2013, she expressed her interest of starting her own business to her husband and thus she being fully supported by appellant and his family, started a business venture under the brand name "Earthling" with the assistance of resources of the company and the appellant and expenses of business of respondent No. 3 were borne by the company. It is stated that relationship between appellant and respondent No. 3 was like a father-daughter relationship. 7. It is further stated that later on, one arrangement was agreed upon between the parties and it was agreed that respondent No. 3 shall shut down "Earthling" venture and she was inducted in company. It is stated that at the time of her induction in the company, respondent no. 3 became greedy and started pressuring Late Mr. Harith Budhraja and appellant to make her one of the Directors in the company and succumbing to immense pressure created by respondent No. 3 on his son, the appellant had no other option but to reluctantly accept his late son's request for keeping his marriage peaceful and thus respondent No. 3 was introduced as a Director in the company on 30.04.2019. 8. It is stated that unfortunately, during 2 nd Covid-19 wage, Late Mr. Harith Budhraja contracted the said virus which gradually deteriorated his health and on 02.05.2021, on being informed about the increasingly depleting health of Late Mr. Harith Budhraja, the appellant and his wife rushed Also At vs Office Of The District Magistrate on 31 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181077684/ 2 back to Delhi but unfortunately Mr. Harith Budhraja passed away on the same day, minutes before they could land in Delhi. It is stated that during such tough times, when the entire family was emotionally shattered, within 5 days of demise of Mr. Harith Budhraja, on 08.05.2021, the respondent No. 3 provided a handwritten statement titled "Definites" to the appellant through whatsapp message images stating all her financial and domestic demands from the appellant and family and she started expressing impatience on division of personal and professional assets and started demanding immediate action on the same. 9. It is further averred that around 09.11.2021, the respondent No. 3 reached to Mr. Naresh Khanna, Company's Chartered Accountant, confidante of the appellant as well as respondent No. 3, requesting him to mediate a settlement between the respondent No. 3 and appellant and in the interest of parties, Mr. Khanna agreed to mediate and undertook several rounds of conversations between the parties to assist them to arrive at a logical conclusion. It is stated that during mediation, despite sharing a cordial familiar relationship, the respondent No. 3 started holding the appellant and his family for ransom and insisted upon discussing monetary compensation, division, partition and settlement of assets of not only her late husband but of the entire family business and personal assets of the appellant and his family members. 10. It is stated that mediation between the party was failing at this point due to unscrupulous demands of respondent No. 3. It is stated that respondent No. 3 through her legal counsel Mr. Ankit Majumdar vide e-mail dated 27.01.2022, demanded Rs. 80,00,00,000/- from appellant and Mr. Ankit Majumdar verbally threatened Mr. Naresh Khanna, that in the event, appellant fails to succumb to demands of respondent No. 3, the they shall be taking necessary action by implicating the appellant and his family members in false and frivolous cases and thus appellant filed a criminal complaint on 29.01.2022 against respondent No. 3 at the Police Headquarters and District Magistrate for seeking protection to threats and blackmail of respondent No. 3. 11. It is stated that notice dated 09.02.2022 was issued whereby extra ordinary general meeting (EGM) was scheduled but respondent No. 3 on various occasions delayed the proceedings on one pretext and other and thus owing to immense delay in conducting EGM, the board of Directors had no other option but to proceed with said EGM wherein the majority shareholders of company voted in favour of agenda and accordingly, the resolution for removal of respondent No. 3 was passed, after following due procedure as provided under the Companies Act 2013. 12. Pursuant to removal of respondent No. 3 from Directorship of company, a bogus complaint of oppression and mismanagement was raised on 25.05.2022 which carried the first allegations of sexual harassment without any specifics or any proof. In the complaint itself, she made monetary claims and compensation towards the company which itself is against the tenet of POSH Act and seeking compensation by threatening to make a complaint under POSH Act is a gross violation of Act and conduct of respondent No. 3 was grossly illegal with a malafide intent. It is stated that purported complaint is clearly an act of extortion and arm twisting and more particularly, a manipulative, fabricated and concocted story as an afterthought of the alleged acts of sexual harassment. It is stated that detailed response to the said legal notice dated 25.05.2022 was sent by appellant to respondent No. 3 vide reply to legal notice dated 11.07.2022 thereby denying all the Also At vs Office Of The District Magistrate on 31 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181077684/ 3 bogus allegations. 13. It is further averred that respondent No. 3 submitted her purported complaint to LCC on 10.06.2022. it is stated that appellant received the first version of complaint made under POSH Act through e-mail on 29.07.2022 which consisted of 34 pages and in fact the attachment received by appellant was only 28 pages and the pages which were sent were illegible. Later on second version of complaint was supplied to appellant on 10.08.2022 by respondent No. 2 which contained 11 pages and same was entirely different from the contents of first complaint. It is stated that thereafter also, despite various communications sent via e-mail to respondent, the appellant has not been provided the legible copies of the complaint and some pages are still missing. It was also stated that respondent No. 2 acted in bias, prejudice, arbitrary manner and in contravention of Rule 7 (2) of the POSH Rules by not providing the complete copy of complaint. It was also stated that appellant was denied an opportunity to cross-examine the witness presented by respondent No. 3. It was also averred that respondent No. 2 failed to complete the inquiry within 90 days period as specified U/s 11 (4) of the POSH Act. It was also stated that respondent No. 2 has taken no advice from the counsel and on completion of the conversation with respondent No. 3, on 29.06.2022, on request from her and legal counsel, the LCC agreed to have an introduction with the counsel and the legal counsel approached the LCC to assist in prompt relief and action for this case. It was also stated that right to seek justice and legal aid is a basic human right of any citizen of the country and respondent No. 3 was advised to exercise her right as she thinks best, for her case and respondent No. 2 informed the legal counsel of the respondent No. 3 that they will conduct the POSH investigation as per due process of POSH Act 2013. It was also averred that respondent ensured that the appellant received all the necessary attention and information to ensue that fair process of investigation is carried out. The other contents of appeal were denied by respondent No. 2. 19. Separate reply was filed by respondent No. 3 to the appeal stating that appellant has not approached this Tribunal with clean hands and the subjects related to inheritance, succession and directorship of respondent No. 3 are irrelevant in the present proceedings and beyond the scope of present appeal. It was also stated that LCC has passed the final order only after proper application of mind towards all the evidences Also At vs Office Of The District Magistrate on 31 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181077684/ 5 that were brought on record by both the parties and thus proper procedure as laid down under the POSH Act and Rules 2013 were followed. The other contents mentioned in appeal were denied by respondent No. 3 and it was prayed that appeal may be dismissed. 21. Rejoinder was filed on behalf of appellant to the reply filed by respondents No. 3 wherein contents of appeal were reiterated and those of reply were denied. 22. It is observed that an application on behalf of appellant U/s 340 Cr. P. C. is also pending on record for initiating criminal proceedings against the respondent No. 3 for perjury and deliberately and willfully making false statement before the court.
texts.arguments: 14. It is pleaded in appeal that complaint is not maintainable as it is barred by limitation as per section 9 (1) of the POSH Act, 2013 and it is stated that as per complaint, the time line of the purported acts of the sexual harassment as alleged by the respondent No. 3 started from 07.05.2021, onwards, however the complaint was only filed by the respondent No. 3 on 10.06.2022 which is almost after a year when the first alleged incident is claimed to have taken place. It is stated that complaint should have been filed within a period of 90 days as per Section 9 (1) of POSH Act and since there was a delay of 145 days on the part of respondent No. 3 in filing the complaint, thus the present complaint was barred by limitation and was not maintainable. It is stated that respondent No. 3 during her tenure in the company has been in the position of chairperson of ICC for nearly 3 years and as the Chairperson of ICC, she must have requisite knowledge about the POSH Act and the time line associated with POSH Act. 15. It is further pleaded in appeal that as per Rule 7 (6) of the POSH Rules, 2013, the parties are not allowed to bring any legal practitioner to represent them at any stage of proceedings before the LCC or ICC, however, as per first date of proceedings before LCC dated 29.06.2022, the respondent No. 3 was accompanied by her legal counsel before the respondent No. 2 and thus, it raised question of bias and prejudice of LCC against the appellant. 16. Various grounds have been raised in the appeal to the effect that respondent No. 2 has failed to comply with the provisions laid under Rule 7 (4) of the POSH Rules and respondent No. 2 failed to provide fair and equal opportunity to appellant to place his defence on record. 17. That being aggrieved by recommendation of ICC, the appellant approached this Tribunal under relevant provisions of Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013 and sought relief as prayed in prayer clause of appeal. 18. Respondent no. 2 filed reply to the appeal of the appellant wherein it has been contended that respondent No. 2 has considered the section 9 of the POSH Act carefully before initiating the Also At vs Office Of The District Magistrate on 31 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181077684/ 4 investigation of POSH Complaint received and assured there is no violation of that. It was also stated that respondent No. 3 was subjected to a series of sexual harassment incidents during the course of employment by appellant and the last incident which further substantiates that respondent No. 3 was subjected to sexual harassment at workplace was her removal from the employment of company dated 20.05.2022. It was also stated that Ld. LCC under proviso two of section 9 has complete power to extend and/or to condone delay caused by the complainant in filing the requisite complaint. Therefore, even if the last incident of sexual harassment was considered to have occurred on 16.01.2022, the complaint was duly registered in compliance with Section 9 of the Posh Act, 2013 as the Ld. LCC has powers to extend the time limit by 3 more months under provision two of Section 9 after the expiration of original period of 3 months. It was also stated that LCC can be constituted with a minimum of 3 members including a Presiding Officer or Chairperson, as the case may be and averments made by the appellants pertaining to constitution of quorum of LCC are absolutely false and baseless. 20. It was also stated in reply that any averments made by the appellant regarding 'no-work-from-home' are concocted and false and despite being a residential property, the said premises was majorly used for business purposes in light of the previously on going pandemic of Covid-19. It was also stated that respondent No. 3 was subjected to sexual harassment multiple times and that the incidents of sexual harassment have happened during the course of respondent No. 3's employment at the premises of company and the premises of extended workplace and appellant is falsely stating that the place where one incident out of multiple incidents has occurred is the residence and not a workplace. It was also contended that respondent No. 3 was examined alone and legal counsel has no role to play whatsoever in the proceedings and the legal counsel of respondent No. 3 had merely just accompanied her to provide assistance, if required. It was also stated that LCC did not entertain the legal counsel and maintained the sanctity of POSH Act, 2013. It was also stated that relationship between the respondent No. 3 and appellant being of a daughter in law and father in law has no bearing on the present case as the sexual harassment incident was committed by the appellant in the capacity of an employer i.e. Chairman and fellow director of the company on the pretext of discussing company matters with respondent No. 3. In the application, it has been pleaded that while arguments were being addressed on stay application filed by appellant, whereby on a specific query by the court, the complainant categorically stated that she had not filed any complaint or any report against the appellant or any of his family members and further she had not relied upon the recommendations of the orders dated 14.02.2023 passed by LCC before any other forum which order was already under challenge before this court. 23. It is further averred in application that it has come to the knowledge of appellant that complainant had already filed criminal complaint under section 156 (3) of Cr. P. C. which is pending before the court of Ms. Anamika, Ld. M. M, Patiala House Courts, relying upon the recommendations of orders dated 14.02.2023 passed by LCC which fact has been willfully and deliberately concealed by complainant from the court and she has committed the offences U/s 340 Cr. P. C., hence, the application was moved in this regard by appellant. 24. In response to said application, the reply was filed by respondent No. 3 to the effect that appellant has filed this application by twisting the real facts of the case which makes it evident that the real intent of the appellant to move this application is not to discuss the merits o the present appeal but just to do frivolous litigation and to delay the proceedings and investigation and thus the present application is outrightly liable to be dismissed. It is further stated that it is the legal right of the respondent No. 3 to knock the doors of any suitable forum to immediately act on the recommendations of LCC report dated 14.02.2023 to seek the appropriate reliefs. It was also stated that respondent No. 3 has made no such statement pertaining to not filing of any complaint against the appellant or his family and instead the respondent No. 3 vide reply dated 06.07.2023 to the main appeal has brought on record the criminal complaint filed by the respondent No. 3 U/s 156 (3) Cr. P. C. against the appellant before the Patiala House Court, New Delhi. Hence, it was prayed that present application may be dismissed and cost may be levied on appellant. 26. Before proceeding to decide the application, this Tribunal would like to mention the relevant extract of Section 340 Cr. P. C. which is reproduced herein below: "Procedure in cases mentioned in Section 195 Also At vs Office Of The District Magistrate on 31 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181077684/ 6 - (1) When, upon an application made to it in this behalf or otherwise, any court is of opinion that it is expedient in the interest of justice that an inquiry should be made into any offence referred to in clause (b) of sub-section (1) of Section 195, which appears to have been committed in or in relation to a proceeding in that court or as the case may be in respect of a document produced or given in evidence in a proceeding in that court, such court may, after such preliminary inquiry, if any as it thinks necessary....'. 33. ICC in its report has made following conclusion and recommendations:- "Conclusion of case : The LCC confirms and concludes that the complainant was sexually harassed by the respondent on 16.01.2022. Recommendations: For the Complainant: i. Advises the complainant to immediately file a police complaint against the respondent under relevant sections of the IPC, if she wishes to pursue a criminal case. ii. Advises the complainant to file a domestic incident report with the respective Protection Officer and request for residence orders and other interim relief. It is further argued that even if the date of last purported incident of sexual harassment was to be considered, which is 16.01.2022, the purported complaint should have been made on or before 18.04.2022 that is within a period of 90 days as per Section 9 (1) of the POSH Act and thus the complaint is barred by limitation and is not maintainable. 36. The respondent has totally denied the arguments in its reply and argued that Ld. LCC under proviso two of Section 9 has complete power to extend or to condone the delay caused by the complainant in filing the complaint. 37. In this regard, reliance is placed upon judgment passed by Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Tejinder Kaur Vs. Union of India and Ors, having W.P. (C) No. 5928/2016 wherein it was held as under:- "Undoubtedly, in terms of second proviso to Section 9 (1) of the Act, the ICC or the Local Committee may for the reasons recorded in writing, extend the time limit, if it is satisfied that there were circumstances, which prevented the woman from filing a complaint. However, such period can only be extended for a further period of three months. 39. Another argument raised by counsel for appellant is that there is a violation of POSH Act and Rules by LCC for permitting the complainant to take legal counsel in proceedings. It is further argued on behalf of appellant that as per Rule 7 (6) of the POSH Rules, 2013, the parties are not allowed to bring any legal practitioner to represent them at any stage of proceedings before the LCC or ICC. 41. Another argument raised by counsel for appellant is regarding validity of the constitution of Local Complaint Committee stating that as per section 7 of POSH Act, the composition of the LCC shall comprise of Chairperson, one member of amongst women working in the municipality in the district, two members from the non-government organization and concern officer dealing with social welfare of women in the district, being member ex-officio and with less than five members on the committee at any given point of time, the LCC becomes defunct and is required to be reconstituted. 42. 46. Another relevant argument raised on behalf of appellant is that LCC erred in its finding by not being able to conclusively distinguish between workplace and domestic disputes between the parties. 47. Contrary to this averment, the respondent No. 3 has argued that despite being a residential property, the said premises was majorly used for business purposes in the light of previously on- going pandemic of Covid-19. It is also argued that respondent No. 3 was subjected to sexual harassment multiple times and that the incidents of sexual harassment have happened during the course of her employment at premises of company and the premises of extended workplace.
